items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to establishing a lymphedema and lymphatic diseases research grants program; and to amend the state finance law, in relation to creating the lymphedema and lymphatic diseases research and education fund
items.lawCode: Add §3153-a, Pub Auth L; add §99-w, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S1058

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to establishing a lymphedema and lymphatic diseases research
grants program; and to amend the state finance law, in relation to
creating the lymphedema and lymphatic diseases research and education
fund

PURPOSE:

To promote greater scientific understanding of lymphedema and
lymphatic disease by establishing a lymphedema and lymphatic disease
research grants program. Grants, not to exceed fifty thousand dollars,
would be awarded on a competitive basis to biomedical research
institutions that are conducting direct research related to lymphedema
and lymphatic disease.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill amends the Public Authorities Law by adding a
new section 3153-a to establish a lymphedema and lymphatic disease
research grants program. This new section lays out how the grants
program shall be administered. It also defines "biomedical research
institution," "lymphedema," and "lymphatic diseases." This new section
also provides that the foundation may adopt rules and regulations to
determine whether an applicant can find other funding, give priority
to those applications for assistance that secure private support for
research or commit new resources to the expansion of this type of
research, and consider the potential long term economic benefits to
the state for awarding the specific grant.  Further, the foundation
has to submit a report to the governor, speaker of the assembly, the
temporary president of the senate and to any other state legislator at
his or her request, a report on the grants program.

Section 2 of this bill amends the State Finance Law by adding a new
section 99-w to create a fund for lymphedema and lymphatic diseases
research and education.

Section 3 of this bill provides that this act shall take effect
immediately.

EXISTING LAW:

Currently, there is no law that provides for a fund for lymphedema and
lymphatic diseases research and education, and there are no grant
programs for such research and education.

JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation would establish a lymphedema and lymphatic disease
research grants program. Grants, not to exceed fifty thousand dollars,
would be awarded on a completive basis to biomedical research
institutions that are conducting direct research related to lymphedema
and lymphatic disease. Lymphedema is an accumulation of lymphatic
fluid in the interstitial tissue that causes swelling, most often in
the arms or legs, and occasionally in other parts of the body.
Lymphedema can develop when lymphatic vessels are missing or impaired


(primary), or when lymph vessels are damaged or lymph nodes removed
(secondary). Radiation therapy, used in the treatment of various
cancers and some AIDS-related diseases, can damage otherwise healthy
lymph nodes and vessels causing scar tissue to form which interrupts
the normal flow of the lymphatic fluid. Moreover, untreated,
lymphedema can lead into a decrease or loss of functioning of the
limbs, skin breakdown, and chronic infections. In the most severe
cases, untreated lymphedema can develop into a rare form of lymphatic
cancer. This legislation would provide much need funding to those
involved in direct research of lymphedema or lymphatic diseases. These
diseases are far more common than society
 notes; however, funding for research has historically not kept pace
to the dramatically growing need for it.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014: S.3072 - Referred to Commerce, Economic Development, and Small
Business
2013: S.3072 - Referred to Commerce, Economic Development, and Small
Business
2012: S.882A - Referred to Corporations, Authorities, and Commissions
2011: S.882A - Referred to Corporations, Authorities, and Commissions
2010: S.2585A - Referred to Corporations, Authorities, and Commissions
2009: S.2585A - Referred to Corporations, Authorities, and Commissions
2008: S.4266A - 3rd Reading Calendar
2007: S.4266A - 3rd Reading Calendar

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Subject to available appropriations.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 213

TO THE SENATE:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:

Senate Bill Number 1058, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to amend the public authorities law, in relation to estab-
      lishing  a  lymphedema  and  lymphatic  diseases  research  grants
      program; and to amend the state finance law, in relation to creat-
      ing  the  lymphedema and lymphatic diseases research and education
      fund"

    NOT APPROVED

  This bill would establish  a  new  Lymphedema  and  Lymphatic  Disease
Research Grants Program. The bill's goal is laudable and I fully support
existing  efforts by the Department of Health to disseminate information
on lymphedema related to cancer treatment, including information on  the
condition,  symptoms,  and treatment of the disease, as well as informa-
tion on support organizations and links to professional associations and
lymphedema therapists.

  Additionally, the 2015-2016 Budget includes  funding  to  support  the
National  Lymphatic  Disease  Patient  Registry and Tissue Bank in their
ongoing efforts to collect biological materials from patients (blood and
tissue samples) that serve as  a  source  for  clinical  and  laboratory
studies of lymphatic diseases. The database is an important resource for
health  care  professionals  who  are  engaged  in  the  identification,
categorization, treatment and prevention of lymphatic diseases.

  In this instance, however, no funds were appropriated to pay  for  the
grants to be awarded under the Program. The bill also identifies the New
York State Foundation for Science, Technology and Innovation to adminis-
ter  the  program, but the foundation is not housed in the Department of
Health and does not have the qualifications or  expertise  necessary  to
peer  review  and  select  the  type  of research grants proposed in the
Program. Accordingly, while I am constrained to disapprove the bill  for
these  reasons,  I  plan to work with the bill's sponsors on how best to
encourage and fund research  opportunities  to  address  lymphedema  and
lymphatic  disease.  I  am further directing the Department of Health to
continue to explore opportunities for additional outreach and  education
in these areas.

  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
